title: Canonical Physics Constants Module
description: Single source of truth for all Kienzle/Taylor/material/thermal constants. Creates src/physics/constants.ts with canonical data and functions used by all pipeline engines, eliminating physics fragmentation across 8+ engines with divergent constant values.

units.title: Create src/physics/constants.ts with canonical data
units.description: Create src/physics/constants.ts containing CANONICAL_KIENZLE (6 ISO groups P/M/K/N/S/H with validated kc1_1/mc from Sandvik/Kennametal datasheets), CANONICAL_TAYLOR (C/n per ISO group), CANONICAL_MATERIAL_DB (13+ materials with all physics props: kc1_1, mc, C, n, k_thermal, sigma_y, density, hardness_HB, vc_base_rough, vc_base_finish), CANONICAL_TOOL_MODULUS (E modulus by tool material: carbide=600GPa, HSS=210GPa, ceramic=380GPa, CBN=680GPa, PCD=850GPa).
acceptance: CANONICAL_KIENZLE has 6 ISO groups with validated kc1_1 and mc values
CANONICAL_TAYLOR has C and n per ISO group
CANONICAL_MATERIAL_DB has 13+ materials with all physics properties
CANONICAL_TOOL_MODULUS has 5 tool materials with correct E modulus values
All types are properly exported with TypeScript interfaces

units.title: Add canonical physics functions
units.description: Add canonical function implementations: kienzleForce(kc1_1, mc, ap, fz) for cutting force, taylorLife(C, n, Vc) implementing T=(C/Vc)^(1/n), toolDeflection(F, L, d, E?) implementing delta=F*L^3/(3*E*I), and boxMullerRNG(seed?) returning a seeded PRNG for reproducible Monte Carlo simulations.
acceptance: kienzleForce computes Fc = kc1_1 * ap * fz^(1-mc) correctly
toolDeflection computes delta = F*L^3/(3*E*I) with cylindrical moment of inertia
boxMullerRNG produces reproducible normal-distributed values from a seed
All functions are exported and documented with JSDoc

units.title: Tests validating dimensional consistency
units.description: Write 15+ tests validating dimensional consistency of all canonical constants and functions. Verify Kienzle force units (N), Taylor life units (min), deflection units (mm), material property ranges, and cross-consistency between related constants.
acceptance: Dimensional consistency verified for all functions (force in N, life in min, deflection in mm)
Material property ranges validated against known physical bounds
